mood: Jhankaradhwani projects a grave, inward, and slightly austere emotional atmosphere. Its tonal material, especially the use of shuddha dhaivata and shuddha nishada, gives it a meditative stillness and devotional seriousness rather than overt brilliance. The raga can suggest quiet yearning, reflective prayerfulness, and a calm but emotionally weighty introspection, drawing the listener inward toward serenity touched by pathos.
description: Jhankaradhwani (also spelled Jhankaradhvani) is the 19th melakarta raga in the Carnatic melakarta system and a sampurna janaka raga, containing all seven swaras in both ascent and descent: S R2 G2 M1 P D1 N1 S / S N1 D1 P M1 G2 R2 S. It belongs to the third chakra, Agni. The swaras employed are chatusruti rishabham, sadharana gandharam, shuddha madhyamam, panchamam, shuddha dhaivatam, and shuddha nishadam. As a melakarta, it serves as a parent scale for derived ragas, though it is itself not among the most frequently heard melas in mainstream concert practice. The available source material also notes an associated name, Jhankarasri, in the extended 108-mela dwi-madhyama panchama-varja scheme, where panchama is omitted and prati madhyama is used in the corresponding parallel mela. Jhankaradhwani is also identified as the shuddha madhyama equivalent of Shamalangi, the 55th melakarta.
gamaka_usage: Jhankaradhwani, though scalar in structure as a melakarta, should not be rendered too plainly, because its identity depends on careful handling of the softer and vivadi-flavored swaras. G2 is best treated with a gentle kampita or nuanced oscillation rather than as a stark plain note; it often needs support from neighboring R2 and M1 to sound settled. D1 and especially N1 require sensitive intonation and are usually more effective with restrained oscillation or subtle nokku/kampita than with flat delivery, since these swaras strongly shape the raga’s grave color. R2 may take mild emphasis and can be approached with slight grace from S or G2. M1 and P act as comparatively stable nyasa points and can be held more steadily to anchor phrases. In descent, smooth jaru movement through N1-D1-P and P-M1-G2-R2 helps preserve continuity and avoids a skeletal scale-like effect. Phrases should balance linear melakarta clarity with measured gamaka weight; over-bright briga-heavy treatment can weaken the raga’s introspective character. Compared with more luminous melas, Jhankaradhwani benefits from a sober, weight-conscious approach in which G2, D1, and N1 are shaded carefully and never rendered harshly.
notable_features: Jhankaradhwani is a melakarta raga and therefore a parent raga in the Carnatic system. It uses the swaras R2, G2, M1, D1, and N1 in addition to S and P. It belongs to the Agni chakra and is the shuddha madhyama equivalent of Shamalangi (55th melakarta). Based on the provided source on dwi-madhyama panchama-varja ragas, its corresponding extended 108-mela counterpart is Jhankarasri. In that scheme, the additional ragas take both madhyamas and omit panchama, with prati madhyama replacing panchama. The source attributes the nomenclature of these 36 extended ragas to Tanjavur S. Kalyanaraman, who developed the dwi-madhyama panchama-varja ragams within that framework.
